subject: general
question: A receipt that does NOT lead to a claim on the government is known as a ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**revenue receipt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A revenue receipt is a receipt that does not create a liability or lead to a claim on the government.
 
• Revenue receipts include tax revenues and non-tax revenues.
 
• Examples of revenue receipts are income tax, corporate tax, and dividends from public sector undertakings.
 
• These receipts are recurring and received during the normal course of government operations.
 
• Revenue receipts are part of the government’s revenue budget and are used to meet its day-to-day operational expenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Government Receipts:**

 
 
• **Revenue Receipts:** Receipts that do not create any liabilities or result in a reduction of assets.
 
• **Capital Receipts:** Receipts that create liabilities or result in a reduction of assets, such as loans raised by the government.
 
 
 
• **Tax Revenue:**
 
 
• Includes income tax, corporate tax, customs duties, excise duties, and GST.
 
• Tax revenue is a major component of revenue receipts.
 
 
 
• **Non-Tax Revenue:**
 
 
• Includes interest receipts, dividends and profits from public sector enterprises, and fees and fines.
 
• Non-tax revenue is also an important source of revenue receipts for the government.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Budget:**
 
 
• Part of the government budget that deals with revenue receipts and revenue expenditures.
 
• Revenue expenditures are those that do not create assets or reduce liabilities.
